# ONNX model authoring

For durable account-backed work, use authenticated MCP and preserve the exact
ONNX artifact and checksum through an opaque fetched resource ID or another
server-supported artifact reference. Do not embed model bytes in generated JSON.
For deliberately local or offline work, keep the artifact and checksum in the
local project and use the local Biosimulant CLI (`biosimulant`); do not claim a Gateway revision,
run, or Passport. Record model origin, training-data claims that are actually
supported, ONNX opset, runtime version, hardware needs, preprocessing,
postprocessing, class labels, and tensor names/dtypes/shapes.

Expose deliberate typed ports rather than raw ambiguous tensors. Test graph loading, input validation, deterministic fixtures where applicable, output shape and label mapping, unsupported operators, and CPU/GPU behavior. Distinguish technical graph execution from biological validation. Run calibration or reference comparisons when requested; return measured outputs.

A finite ONNX wrapper uses `execute(inputs, *, context)` with the imported enum
member `ExecutionPolicy.ONCE_BEFORE_RUN`. Do not use the quoted uppercase string
`"ONCE_BEFORE_RUN"`; its literal runtime value is `"once_before_run"`.




Scientific qualification is removed. Legacy profile metadata is descriptive. Documents, evidence, reference fixtures and visualizations are not platform prerequisites. Preserve real execution errors, scoped authorization and files. File-only work needs no chart. For 0.0.38+, report inner failures with ExecutionOutcome through report_execution_outcome.
